Home, The What Needs You Panel. From “What Needs You”.

What Needs You is where the world tells you things and asks you things. A notice says what happened: groceries you couldn’t pay for, a commitment you slept through, a welcome to the school. It’s asking you at 70/100 and it wants an answer in 2 months.

You owe $791.70 on $4.50 of income. File by April 15, 2027.

The taxes side of things put it in front of you 2d 6h ago, at 70/100 — above the ordinary run of things. If the same thing comes up again the figure only ever goes up: the higher of the two stands, and nothing brings it back down. It’s the only thing waiting on you.

It closes when you answer it, here or on its own screen, or on its date: once April 15, 2027 passes it closes itself, answered or not, because whatever raised it already said where it ends. The world only looks in every two days, so the closing lands at the next look and not on the stroke. Six months after it closes the save keeps no record of it.

Home puts File It and Dismiss against it, and a way through to the screen where it lives, and pressing one of those is doing it. They’re the doing; this is the reading.

How This Works

Chase Total Checking at Chase, $13,510. Primary.

Your wages and other payments are paid into it. Your everyday card’s autopay pays from it.

The primary account is where your debit card’s everyday purchases come from it; cash from a machine comes out of it; bills you pay by hand come from it; a new standing order or autopay starts from it. Making another primary moves nothing already set up.

How This Works

Wages and other payments go to Chase Total Checking: a change reaches Yale’s payroll in 7 days, about one of its weekly pay cycles, as Yale says, and other payers in 14, SLATE’s estimate (employers say one to two pay cycles).

How This Works
Open An Account At Another Bank
How This Works

Sources And Estimates

Chase refuses to authorize any transaction once a card is reported lost or stolen, and sends a replacement card with a new number; for a credit card the account itself stays open and keeps its age for credit reporting.

Chase monitors cards around the clock and may contact the customer by text message, push notification, email or phone call to confirm whether unusual activity was authorized; fraud alerts are automatic and need no enrollment. Chase can refuse to authorize a transaction it reasonably believes may be fraudulent, but doesn’t say it holds a payment pending the customer's reply.

The law, for the debit card: Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act's Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.6(b), a consumer who reports a lost or stolen debit card within two business days of learning of it owes at most the lesser of $50 or the transfers made before notice; after two business days the cap rises to $500. Transfers shown on a periodic statement that aren't reported within 60 days of the statement being sent carry unlimited liability for transfers after that 60-day window. The 2- and 60-day clocks run from different starts: learning of the loss, and the statement's transmittal.

For the credit card: Truth in Lending Act, Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(b)(1)(ii): a cardholder's liability for unauthorized credit card use is capped at the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained before the card issuer is notified.

A payment reported as not yours: Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.11: the bank must decide within 10 business days (20 for a new account's first 30 days); if it takes longer it must provisionally credit the account within 10 business days and may take up to 45 days, or 90 days for point-of-sale debit card, out-of-state or new-account transfers. Results go to the consumer within 3 business days of finishing.

How This Works

From January 1, 2027, Medi-Cal asks for $580.00 of income, time at the School or an exception in the month before you apply, and last month had none of them. It’s outside open enrollment, November 1 to January 15, and you haven’t lost cover in the last 60 days. On a low month’s income, Medicaid (Medi-Cal in California, HUSKY D in Connecticut) takes you at 138% of the poverty line, in New York the Essential Plan to 200%, and in Connecticut Covered Connecticut to 175% of the year before’s, at any time and with no premium; Covered Connecticut is for an income over HUSKY D’s line, whatever your status, and comes with the premium tax credit, from 100% of the poverty line; from 2027 a student in F-1 status or a graduate on OPT has none. From 2027 Medicaid’s work rules are met by a month you spend any of at the School, or one with $580.00 of income (pay, interest, a benefit or a pension): in Connecticut the month before you apply, and any one of the 6 months before a renewal. Being 65 or over, SNAP received under its work rules, or a stay in hospital you ask for counts as meeting them. Short of it, a notice gives 30 days from its receipt to answer before an application is denied or cover ends, and an ending is said 10 days or more ahead, at a month’s end. You pay the whole premium each month, and the return gives back what’s over your share of income, a nonresident’s 1040-NR too: none over 400% of the poverty line, since the enhanced credits ended with 2025. In California a month without cover costs its penalty on the return: the greater of $950.00 a year and 2.5% of income, a twelfth a month, to $420.00; 1 this year so far.

Applying for Medi-Cal anyway, you’re sent a notice of noncompliance and 30 days from its receipt to show the work rules met in January 2027, or an exception, a stay in hospital that month among them; it’s decided after, and the marketplace sells to you meanwhile.
